mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future earnings, lowering the present value of equity expectations and driving negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the tightening phase, with a p-value > 0.05 in a two-sample test against the pre-tightening period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, prompting risk-on sentiment and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same or
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day ahead returns are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05), or the correlation between PAYEMS momentum and SPX returns is below 0.3.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 3% suggests accelerating consumer demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 3% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or the change in SPX 5-day returns is not statistically significant relative to the prior month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side constraints, which amplifies demand imbalances and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by more than 5% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant correlation between INDPRO declines and SPX 20-day returns (Pearson's rho < 0.2, p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5% and the CPIAUCSL inflation rate remains below 2%, market participants interpret this as a 'soft landing,' prompting risk-on positioning that drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% and CPIAUCSL < 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or the joint significance test of UNRATE and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is below 0.05 (F-test).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining worker participation in the labor force (PAYEMS < previous month for three months) suggests a loss of demand, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05) or the regression coefficient on PAYEMS is positive and significant (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising FEDFUNDS above 6% indicate aggressive policy tightening, which increases real interest rates and dampens equity valuation multiples, resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.5 percentage points in two consecutive months and remains above 6%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or the change in the SPX 5-day return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer confidence (not directly observable in the provided proxies) would typically precede a supply shock, but here we proxy it via a sudden, unexplained spike in RSAFS (retail sales) followed by a collapse in INDPRO within a week, suggesting disrupted supply chains that precede a short-term negative 20-day SPX return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS spikes by >10% in a week and INDPRO declines by >8% in the following week
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or the Granger causality test from RSAFS to SPX returns is not significant (p > 0.1).
